boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Rose-Hulman rituals, objects, and recurring campus events with clear, public-facing evidence.

cards.title: Homecoming Bonfire
cards.subtitle: Annual Homecoming tradition
cards.notes: View the Bonfire Field only from permitted areas and follow event staff directions; the official tradition page describes its annual Homecoming role.
cards.short_summary: First-year students build Rose-Hulman’s annual Homecoming bonfire.
cards.evidence_claim: Rose-Hulman identifies the annual bonfire held before the Homecoming football game as a campus tradition.
cards.access_notes: Construction and event access are controlled by the institute; observe only from approved public areas.

cards.title: The Bonfire Outhouse
cards.subtitle: Named feature of the Homecoming structure
cards.notes: Photograph the outhouse from a designated public viewing area when it is displayed; do not enter construction zones or touch the structure.
cards.short_summary: An old wooden outhouse is placed atop the student-built bonfire structure.
cards.evidence_claim: Rose-Hulman states that the freshman-built bonfire includes an old wooden outhouse on top, with a football-win belief tied to its fall.
cards.access_notes: View only during publicly accessible Homecoming programming and obey all safety barriers.

cards.title: Rosie the Elephant
cards.subtitle: Rose-Hulman mascot tradition
cards.notes: Look for Rosie at public campus or athletic events and take a photo without interrupting mascot appearances or event operations.
cards.short_summary: Rosie is the elephant mascot woven into Rose-Hulman’s campus tradition.
cards.evidence_claim: Rose-Hulman describes Rosie the elephant as its school mascot for more than 100 years and part of its storied history.
cards.access_notes: Mascot appearances vary by event; use public event schedules to plan a visit.

cards.title: Dear Old Rose
cards.subtitle: Rose-Hulman fight song
cards.notes: Listen for the song at a public school event, and use the official lyrics page rather than assuming a particular performance schedule.
cards.short_summary: “Dear Old Rose” is Rose-Hulman’s published fight song.
cards.evidence_claim: Rose-Hulman’s culture-and-tradition page names “Dear Old Rose” as the institution’s fight song and publishes its lyrics.
cards.access_notes: Public performances depend on the event schedule.

cards.title: Orientation Sidewalk Send-Off
cards.subtitle: Residence Life welcome ritual
cards.notes: If visiting during orientation, stay in public areas and do not enter participant-only sessions; the send-off occurs after the final presentation.
cards.short_summary: Residence Life staff line the sidewalks and applaud new students as orientation concludes.
cards.evidence_claim: Rose-Hulman documents that Residence Life staff line sidewalks and applaud students leaving their final freshman-orientation presentation.
cards.access_notes: Orientation activities can be restricted to incoming students and invited guests.

cards.title: Commencement Bagpipe Parade
cards.subtitle: Graduation-day campus procession
cards.notes: Watch from public commencement viewing areas and follow road-closure guidance; graduates begin their procession from Hatfield Lawn.
cards.short_summary: Graduates return to the orientation location and begin their Commencement parade led by bagpipes.
cards.evidence_claim: Rose-Hulman says graduates meet at the same location used at orientation and start their parade to Commencement led by bagpipes.
cards.access_notes: The 2026 commencement schedule lists graduates departing Hatfield Lawn; follow event and roadway instructions.

cards.title: Greatest Floor Competition
cards.subtitle: Residence-hall 24-hour challenge
cards.notes: Check Residence Life programming before attending; take photos only where participants and organizers allow, especially during active challenges.
cards.short_summary: Residence-hall floors compete across 24 events held over 24 hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Rose-Hulman documents Greatest Floor as a residence-hall competition involving 24 events over 24 hours, begun in 2011.
cards.access_notes: Participation is residence-life based; verify the current program and visitor access.

cards.title: The Rose Show
cards.subtitle: Annual student-project showcase
cards.notes: Visit the Sports and Recreation Center during the announced showcase window and photograph projects only with exhibitor permission.
cards.short_summary: A nearly century-old Rose-Hulman showcase of student projects and innovations.
cards.evidence_claim: Rose-Hulman calls the Rose Show a highly anticipated tradition for nearly 100 years and states that its 2026 event was free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: Rose-Hulman to Present Student Innovations at Free, Public Rose Show May 6
cards.access_notes: The cited 2026 event was free and public; confirm future dates and access before visiting.

cards.entity_name: Bikes For Tykes Bicycle Assembly Day
cards.title: Bikes For Tykes Assembly Day
cards.subtitle: Annual campus bicycle-building event
cards.notes: Look for the current assembly-day announcement before attending, and follow organizer instructions around tools, bicycles, and work areas.
cards.short_summary: A recurring Rose-Hulman campus event focused on building bicycles.
cards.evidence_claim: Rose-Hulman lists Bikes For Tykes’ Bicycle Assembly Day among its biggest annual non-athletic campus activities.
cards.source_title: Sports and Recreation Center Celebrating 25 Years of Serving Campus & Community
cards.access_notes: Confirm whether the current year’s assembly day has public volunteer or visitor access.

cards.title: R Beanies
cards.subtitle: Historical first-year identifier
cards.notes: Treat this as a historical tradition: seek archival images or official history materials rather than presenting it as a current student requirement.
cards.short_summary: By 1920, Rose freshmen wore “R” beanies to mark their first-year status.
cards.evidence_claim: Rose-Hulman’s 2026 Commencement program records that, by 1920, freshmen wore “R” beanies to denote their newcomer status.
cards.access_notes: Historical practice; the cited source does not establish that beanies are currently worn.
